info.title: KPOST KMail API (v5.0)
info.description:
REST API for the KPOST KMail service.

**Identity model** — no endpoint accepts the caller's identity in the request body. The JWT filter resolves the KPOST ID from the `Authorization` header and stores it as the `kpostID` request attribute; controllers then overwrite the corresponding body field (`kpostUser`, `fromAddress`, `kpostID`) before calling the service layer. Any value you send in those fields is ignored.

**Storage** — mail metadata, contacts, groups and settings live in MySQL (JPA). Mail bodies live in the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content`. Attachments live in AWS S3.

**Response envelope** — successful and failed calls alike return a flat `Map<String,Object>` containing `status`, `statusCode`, `urlPath` and usually `data`. Note that several read endpoints return HTTP 500 with an inner `statusCode` of 200/204 when no rows match; the inner `status` field is the reliable success indicator.

tags.name: Storage Quota
tags.description: Reports how much of the user's KLOUD storage allowance is consumed by mail and attachments. Backed by MySQL usage aggregates; attachment sizes originate from AWS S3 object metadata recorded at upload time.

tags.name: Mailbox & Contacts
tags.description: The broadest controller in the service: dashboard/folder listing, follow-up status buckets, unread counts, contact directories, importance and delete flags, and PDF export. Almost everything here reads MySQL only — `KmailMaster`, `KmailTransaction`, `Contacts`, `UserGroup` and `KmailOtherDomainContacts` — returning mail **metadata without bodies**. Bodies live in the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content` and are fetched separately through `v2/readMail`. Listing endpoints are keyset-paginated on `kmailID` rather than offset-paginated: pass the `firstKmailID`/`lastKmailID` returned by the previous page to walk forwards or backwards.

tags.name: Draft Mail
tags.description: Compose-time persistence for unsent mail. Drafts are stored as MySQL `Draft` rows keyed by `kmailID` and owned by the authenticated sender (`fromAddress`), which is always taken from the JWT and never from the payload. Drafts do not create MongoDB content documents — the body is written to `table_kpost_kmail_content` only when the mail is finally posted via `v2/sentMail/postMail`.

tags.name: Read Mail & Attachments
tags.description: Retrieval of mail bodies, reference chains, copy-recipient info and attachment binaries. This is the **primary MongoDB read path**: mail metadata is fetched from MySQL (`KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction`), then `ReadKmailServiceImpl` calls `KmailContentRepository.findByKmailID(long)` against the `table_kpost_kmail_content` collection to load the actual body, forward note and attachment names. Attachment and media bytes are streamed from AWS S3 by UUID. Opening a mail is not a pure read — it also flips the recipient's read status in MySQL.

tags.name: Sent Mail
tags.description: Outbound mail: single sends, bulk campaigns and other-domain delivery. This is the **only** controller that writes to MongoDB — `SentMailServiceImpl` splits each outgoing mail into a MySQL `KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction` metadata record (one transaction row per recipient) and a `table_kpost_kmail_content` document holding the heavy body, forward note and attachment names, linked by the numeric `kmail_id`. Attachment binaries go to AWS S3. The sender is always taken from the JWT.

tags.name: Sent Mail (Legacy Path)
tags.description: Legacy un-versioned alias kept for older mobile clients. Mapped at `/sentMail` rather than `/v2/sentMail`, it exposes a single multipart send that is byte-for-byte equivalent to `POST /v2/sentMail/postMailMultiPart/`. New integrations should target the v2 controller; this one exists only so shipped clients keep working.

tags.name: Translation
tags.description: Language detection and mail-body translation, plus two send endpoints retained from an earlier design. **This whole controller is `permitAll`** in `SecurityConfiguration` (`/v2/translator/**`), so none of its operations receive a `kpostID` from the JWT filter — including `postMail`, which sends real mail using the `fromAddress` supplied in the request body.

tags.name: KMail Settings
tags.description: Per-user personalisation: digital signature, canned instant replies, salutations, letterheads and the structured mail signature. Everything here is stored in MySQL on the `UsersKmailSetting` row for the authenticated `kpostID` — the composite `mailSignature` and `letterHead` values are JSON columns on that relational row, **not** MongoDB documents. Letterhead and signature images are held in AWS S3. Every operation scopes itself to the JWT-resolved user; none accepts a target account as input.

post.summary: [Dead Code] Post a Mail from a MIME Message
post.description:
**Do not use.** Retained only so the route does not disappear from older builds; it cannot succeed.

The handler declares `MimeMessage msg = null` and passes that null straight into `TranslationService.postMailMimeMsg`, so the MIME source it is supposed to send is never populated. The `unused` prefix on the path reflects that it is unreferenced by any client.

**Database behaviour** — nominally the same MySQL + MongoDB write path as a normal send, but in practice the call fails before persisting anything.

500.description: Expected outcome — the null `MimeMessage` causes the service call to fail.

post.summary: Detect Source Language and Translate Mail Text
post.description:
**Use this when** the user clicks "Translate" on a mail body or composes in a second language.

**Behaviour** — if `langFrom` is omitted the source language is auto-detected first by calling the external **detectlanguage.com** API, then the text is translated into `langTo`. When the resolved `langFrom` equals `langTo` the request is rejected rather than returning the text unchanged.

**Database behaviour** — none. This endpoint performs outbound HTTP to third-party translation services and touches neither MySQL nor MongoDB; nothing is persisted, so translations are not cached and repeat calls re-bill the provider.

**Security note** — the operation is `permitAll` and the detectlanguage API key is hardcoded in the handler, so an unauthenticated caller can consume the project's translation quota. Treat this endpoint as publicly reachable and consider moving the key into configuration.

requestBody.description: `msgToTranslate` and `langTo` are required. Omit `langFrom` to auto-detect. Language codes are ISO 639-1.

500.description: Source and target languages are identical (`errorValue`: "From language and To language are same."), the translation provider returned nothing, or detection/translation threw.

200.description: `data` holds the `TranslationEntity` with `msgAfterTranslation` and the resolved from/to languages populated.

post.summary: Send a Mail (Unauthenticated Translator Path)
post.description:
**Use this when** an integration must send a translated mail through the translator surface. Delegates to exactly the same `SentMailService.postMail` used by `POST /v2/sentMail/postMail`.

**Database behaviour** — the full send path: a `KmailMaster` row plus one `KmailTransaction` per recipient in MySQL, one body document in the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content`, and SMTP hand-off for external recipients.

**Side effects** — sends real mail and is irreversible.

**Security note** — this differs from every other send endpoint in one important way: it sits under the `permitAll` `/v2/translator/**` matcher and takes **no `HttpServletRequest`**, so `fromAddress` is read verbatim from the request body and never overwritten from a token. A caller can therefore nominate any sender address. Prefer `POST /v2/sentMail/postMail`, which binds the sender to the JWT.

requestBody.description: `fromAddress` is honoured as supplied — it is **not** overwritten from a token on this path.

500.description: Send failed; `errorMsg` carries the raw exception message.

post.summary: Send a Mail (JSON, No New Attachments)
post.description:
**Use this when** the user clicks Send on a mail whose attachments — if any — were already uploaded to S3 and are referenced by `attachmentUuid`. This is the primary send path and also handles replies, forwards, shares and group sends, discriminated by `kmailType` and `groupFlag`.

**Database behaviour** — a multi-store write performed by `SentMailService.postMail`:
1. Inserts a `KmailMaster` row in MySQL plus one `KmailTransaction` row per resolved recipient    (to + cc + bcc, or every member of the group when `groupFlag` is true).
2. Inserts a document into the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content` keyed by the numeric    `kmail_id`, carrying `kmail_content`, `forward_note`, `originalMailDetails` and `attachment_name`.    The body deliberately does **not** live in MySQL.
3. Hands the message to the SMTP layer for recipients outside the KPOST domain.

**Side effects** — sending is irreversible and triggers push notifications. A recipient who has unsubscribed (see `v2/common/saveUnsubscriberDetails`) is skipped. Because the two stores are written without a distributed transaction, a MongoDB failure after the MySQL insert can leave metadata with no retrievable body.

**Note** — this handler returns the service's own `ResponseEntity` unchanged on success, so the envelope shape is produced by `SentMailServiceImpl`; the controller only builds the 500 envelope.

requestBody.description: `kmailType` selects the semantics — 0 normal, 1 reply, 2 share, 15 forward (see `KPOSTConstants`). For replies and forwards set `originalKmailID` / `referenceKmailID`. For group sends set `groupFlag: true` and put the group ID in `toAddress`. `fromAddress` is ignored and overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: Send failed — unresolvable recipient, SMTP failure, or a MySQL/MongoDB write error.

200.description: Mail accepted. Envelope produced by `SentMailService`; `data` carries the per-recipient `SentMailResponseObject` list including the new `kmailID`.

post.summary: Send a Mail with Newly Uploaded Attachments
post.description:
**Use this when** the user attaches files at send time. Functionally identical to `postMail` but accepts the binaries in the same request, avoiding a separate upload step.

**Database behaviour** — files are streamed to AWS S3 first (`sendKmailMultiPartfileUpload`), yielding `KatchupAttachment` handles. Then the same dual write as `postMail`: `KmailMaster` + one `KmailTransaction` per recipient in MySQL, and one `table_kpost_kmail_content` document in MongoDB whose `attachment_name` array records the stored file names.

**Side effects** — S3 objects are written before the mail is persisted, so a later failure leaves orphaned objects. `attachmentFlag` is forced to `1` when a non-empty file is present. Sending is irreversible.

**Request shape** — `multipart/form-data`: a repeated `files` part plus a `text` **form field** holding the JSON-encoded `SentMailRequestObject`.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: JSON-encoded `SentMailRequestObject`, sent as a plain form field rather than a JSON part.

files.description: Attachment binaries. An empty first part (size 0) means 'no attachments' and skips the S3 upload.

500.description: S3 upload failed, `text` was not valid `SentMailRequestObject` JSON, or the service returned an empty recipient list.

post.summary: Send One Mail to Many Recipients (Bulk Campaign)
post.description:
**Use this when** dispatching a newsletter or announcement to a recipient list. Distinct from `postMail` with a long `ccList`: each recipient receives an individual mail with no visibility of the others, and delivery is tracked as a campaign.

**Database behaviour** — fans `toAddressList` out into one `KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction` set per recipient in MySQL, with the shared body written once per mail into the MongoDB `table_kpost_kmail_content` collection. Recipients who previously unsubscribed from this sender are filtered out before dispatch.

**Side effects** — long-running and asynchronous: this call returns once the campaign is accepted, not once every message is delivered. Poll `GET /v2/sentMail/bulkMail/status/{fromAddress}` for progress. Irreversible once accepted.

requestBody.description: `toAddressList` carries the recipient list. `fromAddress` is overwritten from the JWT. Attachments must already exist in S3 and be referenced via `attachmentUuid`.

500.description: Dispatch threw; `errorMsg` carries the raw exception message.

post.summary: Send a Bulk Campaign with an Uploaded Recipient/Attachment File
post.description:
**Use this when** the campaign's recipient list or attachment arrives as an uploaded file rather than as an inline `toAddressList` — for example a CSV export from a CRM.

**Database behaviour** — the uploaded file is processed by `SentMailService.postBulkMailMultipart`, then the same fan-out as `postBulkMail`: one MySQL `KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction` set per recipient, one MongoDB `table_kpost_kmail_content` document per mail, attachment binaries in S3.

**Side effects** — asynchronous and irreversible once accepted; poll `GET /v2/sentMail/bulkMail/status/{fromAddress}` for progress.

**Request shape** — `multipart/form-data` with two parts: a binary `file` part and a `bulkMailRequest` **JSON part** (`Content-Type: application/json`). Note this differs from `postMailMultiPart`, where the JSON travels in a `text` form field instead.

file.description: Campaign input file — recipient list and/or attachment, interpreted by the bulk-mail service.

500.description: File could not be parsed, or dispatch threw; `errorMsg` carries the raw exception message.

post.summary: Echo a Compose Payload (Diagnostic)
post.description:
**Use this when** verifying connectivity or debugging client-side serialisation — the handler simply echoes `fromAddress`, `toAddress` and `kmailContent` back to the caller.

**Database behaviour** — none. No MySQL, no MongoDB, no S3, no SMTP. Nothing is sent and nothing is stored.

**Note** — this path is explicitly `permitAll` in `SecurityConfiguration` (`/v2/sentMail/loadMail/**`), so it is reachable without a token and will echo whatever payload it is given. It is a diagnostic stub, not part of the product surface.

requestBody.description: Any `SentMailRequestObject`; only the three echoed fields are read.

200.description: Echoed payload under the keys `FromAddress:: `, `ToAddress:: ` and `KmailContent:: ` (note the trailing spaces in those key names).

post.summary: Resolve Mail-Server Credentials for a KPOST Account
post.description:
**Use this when** a client needs the SMTP/IMAP settings for an account — typically a native client configuring an outbound session rather than the web UI.

**Database behaviour** — reads the user and mail-configuration rows from MySQL and returns the resolved connection profile. Read-only; no MongoDB involvement.

**Security note** — unlike every other endpoint in this controller, the account here is taken from the request body (`kpostID` + `password`/`token`), not from the JWT. Callers are therefore asserting an identity rather than proving one, and the response carries credential material. Restrict exposure of this operation accordingly.

requestBody.description: Supply `kpostID` together with either `password` or a valid `token`.

500.description: Unknown `kpostID`, rejected credentials, or a lookup failure. All three collapse into the same envelope — the response does not distinguish authentication failure from a server error.

post.summary: Open a Single Mail and Read Its Body
post.description:
**Use this when** the user clicks a message in either the Inbox or the Sent folder — this is the main "open a mail" call. The folder is chosen by `kmailType`: any value containing `sent` routes to the sent-mail reader, everything else is treated as Inbox.

**Database behaviour** — metadata (subject, participants, timestamps, attachment captions) comes from MySQL; the body itself is a direct key lookup on the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content` via `KmailContentRepository.findByKmailID(kmailID)`, which also supplies `forward_note` and `attachment_name`.

**Side effects** — **not idempotent for the Inbox path**: opening an unread mail updates the recipient's read status and unread counters in MySQL, which is what makes subsequent `unOpenedMailCountBySenderID` results change.

**Special handling** — when `selectedContact` contains `mailer-daemon@`, bounce bodies are rewritten to strip `<address>` angle brackets so the client does not render them as broken HTML tags.

requestBody.description: `kmailID` identifies the mail and `kmailType` selects the folder. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: The read threw — MongoDB unreachable, or malformed stored content.

400.description: Nothing resolved for that `kmailID` — no MySQL metadata, or no matching document in `table_kpost_kmail_content`. This is the closest thing to a 'not found' this endpoint returns; it does not emit 404.

200.description: `data` holds the `ReadContentResponseObject` with the body merged from MongoDB.

post.summary: Read the Bodies of an Entire Reference (Thread) Chain
post.description:
**Use this when** the user expands a conversation and the client needs every earlier mail in the thread in one round trip, rather than issuing one `sentAndInboxMailContent` call per message.

**Database behaviour** — for each ID in `referenceMails`, metadata is read from MySQL and the body is then loaded from the MongoDB `table_kpost_kmail_content` collection via `KmailContentRepository.findByKmailID`. Note this is an **N+1 access pattern**: one Mongo round trip per referenced mail, not a single `$in` query — long threads cost proportionally more.

**Side effects** — read-oriented, but the underlying service may mark newly opened messages as read in MySQL as a side effect of materialising them.

requestBody.description: `referenceMails` carries the ordered list of `kmailID`s in the thread. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No reference mails resolved — an empty list, IDs the caller may not read, or MongoDB documents missing for the given `kmail_id`s — or the lookup threw.

200.description: `data` holds a `ReadContentResponseObject` array, one entry per referenced mail.

post.summary: Batch-Fetch Mail Metadata by kmailID
post.description:
**Use this when** the client holds a set of `kmailID`s — from a push notification, a search result or a deep link — and needs their headers (subject, participants, status, attachment flags) without opening each one.

**Database behaviour** — a single batched MySQL read of `KmailMaster` and its `KmailTransaction` children. **Metadata only — no MongoDB access and no bodies.** Call `sentAndInboxMailContent` per mail to obtain the body.

**Authorisation** — the handler walks the transactions and grants access only if the caller is the sender or a receiver of at least one mail in the batch, or if `kmailType == 2` (a share). Be aware the check is **batch-wide, not per-mail**: authorisation on any one mail returns the whole requested set, so callers should not mix IDs across trust boundaries in a single request.

**Side effects** — none; read status is not changed.

requestBody.description: `kmailIDs` carries the numeric IDs to resolve.

200.description: `data` holds the `KmailMaster` array with nested transactions.

500.description: No mails matched, the caller is party to none of them (authorisation failure is reported as 500, not 403), or the query threw.

post.summary: Read a Draft's Saved Body
post.description:
**Use this when** reopening a saved draft in the compose window and the client needs the full body rather than the summary shown in the drafts list.

**Database behaviour** — reads the MySQL `Draft` row identified by `draftKmailID`/`kmailID` for the authenticated owner. **No MongoDB access**: draft bodies live on the MySQL row, because a draft has never been sent and therefore has no `table_kpost_kmail_content` document.

**Side effects** — none; drafts have no read state.

requestBody.description: Identify the draft by `draftKmailID` (or `kmailID`). `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No such draft, the draft belongs to another user, or the read threw.

post.summary: Download an Attachment from an External-Domain Mail
post.description:
**Use this when** the user downloads an attachment on a mail that arrived from outside KPOST, where the file may not yet have been copied into S3 under a KPOST UUID.

**Resolution order** — the handler tries progressively cheaper-to-costlier sources:
1. Loads every row of `AllDomain` from MySQL and checks whether the sender's domain is a known KPOST    domain; if so, resolves the UUID from `KmailMaster.attachmentPath` by matching `targetFileName` and    serves it straight from S3.
2. For group mails (`groupFlag: true`), asks the service for the stored UUID and serves from S3.
3. Otherwise falls back to `downloadODAttachment`, which retrieves the file from the origin mail    server.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL reads (`AllDomain`, `KmailMaster`) plus S3 object reads. No MongoDB access. Step 1 performs a **full-table scan of `AllDomain` on every call** and dereferences the first transaction's sender without a null guard, so a mail with no transactions will fail here.

**Returns raw bytes**, not the JSON envelope used elsewhere in this API.

requestBody.description: `kmailID` plus `targetFileName` identify the attachment. `kmailType` is `@NotBlank` and is validated. Set `groupFlag` for group mails.

500.description: Attachment not found in S3 or on the origin server, the mail has no transactions, or retrieval threw. The body is empty — no diagnostic envelope is returned on this path.

post.summary: Resolve a Mail's Attachment Metadata
post.description:
**Use this when** the client needs the attachment manifest for a mail — file names, captions and the S3 UUIDs — before downloading any bytes.

**Database behaviour** — identical resolution path to `sentAndInboxMailContent`: MySQL metadata plus a `findByKmailID` lookup against the MongoDB `table_kpost_kmail_content` collection, whose `attachment_name` array backs the manifest.

**Note** — despite the name this endpoint returns **JSON, not file bytes**. Take the UUID from the response and call `GET /v2/readMail/download/{uuid}` to fetch the actual binary from S3.

requestBody.description: `kmailID` plus `kmailType` (a value containing `sent` selects the sent folder). `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: `data` holds the `ReadContentResponseObject` including the attachment manifest.

500.description: The lookup threw.

post.summary: Activate One of the User's Letterheads
post.description:
**Use this when** the user picks which uploaded letterhead should be applied to outgoing mail. Activation is exclusive — selecting one deactivates whichever was previously active.

**Database behaviour** — `CommonDao.setLetterHead` flips the active flag inside the `letterHead` JSON array on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, inside a `@Transactional` boundary. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — changes the appearance of all subsequently sent mail. Already-sent mail is unaffected.

requestBody.description: A free-form JSON object; only the `id` key is read — the identifier of a letterhead previously returned by `getAllLetterHead`. The owning user comes from the JWT.

500.description: No such letterhead id for this user, or the update threw.

post.summary: Save the Entire Mail Signature in One Call
post.description:
**Use this when** saving the signature builder wholesale — for example a "Save all" button, or an import/restore flow. This is the bulk equivalent of the five per-block endpoints plus the template selection.

**Database behaviour** — replaces `personalData`, `companyData`, `graphics`, `style` and `socialMedialink` together inside the `mailSignature` JSON column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. No MongoDB access.

**Important** — unlike the per-block endpoints, the top-level blocks here are read directly rather than via `getOrDefault`, so **any block you omit is written as null and its previous contents are lost**. Send the complete signature, or use the per-block endpoints for partial edits. Note also that `templateID` is *not* part of this payload — set it with `saveOrUpdateMailSignatureTemplateId`.

requestBody.description: Top-level keys: `personalData`, `companyData`, `graphics`, `style`, `socialMedialink`. Each holds the same nested keys accepted by the corresponding per-block endpoint.

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Choose the Signature Template Layout
post.description:
**Use this when** the user selects a layout from the gallery returned by `getLetterHeadTemplate`. Only the chosen template's id is stored — the user's own personal, company, graphics, style and social blocks are reused inside whichever layout is active, so switching layouts never loses entered data.

**Database behaviour** — replaces the `templateID` key inside the `mailSignature` JSON column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — changes the rendering of all subsequently composed signatures. The id is stored without checking that a matching `LetterHeadTemplate` exists, so a stale id will fail at render time rather than here.

requestBody.description: Only the `templateID` key is read — an `id` from `getLetterHeadTemplate`.

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Save the Style Block of the Mail Signature
post.description:
**Use this when** the user picks the accent colour and font for their signature.

**Database behaviour** — loads the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, replaces the `style` key inside the `mailSignature` JSON column, and saves. No MongoDB access.

**Field handling** — both keys are read with `getOrDefault(key, "")` and stored verbatim as strings; neither the colour nor the font name is validated, so an invalid value is accepted here and only surfaces as a rendering problem in the composed mail.

requestBody.description: Recognised keys: `color` (typically a CSS hex value) and `fontStyle` (a CSS font family).

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Save the Social Media Links of the Mail Signature
post.description:
**Use this when** the user adds the social profile icons that appear at the foot of their signature.

**Database behaviour** — loads the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, replaces the `socialMedialink` key inside the `mailSignature` JSON column, and saves. No MongoDB access.

**Field handling** — the five recognised keys are read with `getOrDefault(key, "")`, so a network you omit is stored as an empty string, which is how the renderer knows to hide that icon. Send all five every time and blank the ones you want hidden.

**Note** — the stored key is spelled `socialMedialink` (lower-case `l` in "link"); match that exactly when reading the signature back via `getMailSignature`.

requestBody.description: Recognised keys: `twitter`, `facebook`, `instagram`, `linkedIn`, `youTube`. Note the capitalisation of `linkedIn` and `youTube`.

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Save the Personal Block of the Mail Signature
post.description:
**Use this when** the user fills in the "Personal details" tab of the signature builder. The signature is edited one block at a time, so this call replaces only the `personalData` section and leaves company, graphics, style and social links untouched.

**Database behaviour** — loads the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, replaces the `personalData` key inside the `mailSignature` JSON column, and saves. No MongoDB access.

**Field handling** — the six recognised keys are read with `getOrDefault(key, "")`, so any key you omit is stored as an **empty string rather than left at its previous value**. Always send the full block, not a partial patch. Unrecognised keys are silently discarded.

requestBody.description: Recognised keys: `firstName`, `lastName`, `designation`, `emailId`, `mobileNumber`, `alternateMobile`. All are optional and default to an empty string.

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Save the Graphics Block of the Mail Signature
post.description:
**Use this when** the user sets the profile photo and promotional banner shown in their signature, together with the URL the banner links to.

**Database behaviour** — loads the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, replaces the `graphics` key inside the `mailSignature` JSON column, and saves. No MongoDB access.

**Note** — this endpoint stores **URLs only; it does not upload images**. Host the assets first (or upload them elsewhere in the platform) and pass the resulting links here. Keys are read with `getOrDefault(key, "")`, so omitted keys are blanked rather than preserved.

requestBody.description: Recognised keys: `photoUrl`, `bannerUrl`, `bannerLinkingTo`.

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Save the Company Block of the Mail Signature
post.description:
**Use this when** the user fills in the "Company details" tab of the signature builder. Replaces only the `companyData` section of the signature.

**Database behaviour** — loads the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, replaces the `companyData` key inside the `mailSignature` JSON column, and saves. No MongoDB access.

**Field handling** — keys are read with `getOrDefault(key, "")`, so omitted keys are stored as empty strings rather than preserved. Send the whole block on every call.

requestBody.description: Recognised keys: `companyName`, `website`, `addressLine1`, `addressLine2`.

500.description: No `UsersKmailSetting` row exists for this user, or the save threw.

post.summary: Create or Update a Custom Salutation
post.description:
**Use this when** the user adds a greeting ("Dear", "Respected", "Hi") to the dropdown offered by the compose screen, which pairs it with the recipient's name as `saluation` + `saluationName`.

**Database behaviour** — upserts into the `customizedSaluation` JSON column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. Supplying `saluationID` updates in place; omitting it appends. No MongoDB access.

**Note** — "Saluation" is the spelling used throughout the API and the stored payload; it is not a typo you can correct client-side.

requestBody.description: `saluation` carries the greeting text. Include `saluationID` to edit an existing entry. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No settings row for this user (`msg`: "Invalid KpostID"), or the write threw.

post.summary: Create or Update a Canned Instant Reply
post.description:
**Use this when** the user saves a reusable quick reply ("Thanks, received", "Will revert shortly") that later appears as a one-tap option when reading a mail.

**Database behaviour** — upserts into the `customizedInstantReply` JSON column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. Supplying `id` updates that entry in place; omitting it appends a new one. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — overwrites the stored text for an existing `id` without versioning.

requestBody.description: `instantReply` carries the text. Include `id` to edit an existing entry, omit it to create one. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No settings row for this user (`msg`: "Invalid KpostID"), or the write threw.

post.summary: Upload a Letterhead Header and Footer Image Pair
post.description:
**Use this when** the user brands their outgoing mail with a company letterhead. A letterhead is always a **pair** — both parts are required in the same request, so a header cannot be uploaded without its matching footer.

**Database behaviour** — both images are uploaded to AWS S3, then a new entry describing the pair is appended to the `letterHead` JSON array column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — uploading does **not** activate the letterhead. Call `setLetterHead` with the returned id to make it the active one. S3 objects are written before the row is updated, so a later failure can orphan them.

**Request shape** — `multipart/form-data` with two required file parts, `headerFile` and `footerFile`.

headerFile.description: Header image rendered at the top of outgoing mail.

footerFile.description: Footer image rendered at the bottom of outgoing mail.

500.description: S3 upload failed, the settings row is missing, or the update threw. No message is included on this path.

post.summary: Delete an Uploaded Letterhead
post.description:
**Use this when** the user removes a letterhead they no longer want in the picker.

**Database behaviour** — `CommonDao.deleteLetterHead` removes the matching entry from the `letterHead` JSON array on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, scoped to the JWT-resolved user, inside a `@Transactional` boundary. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — destructive and not reversible. If the deleted letterhead was the active one, outgoing mail reverts to no letterhead. The underlying S3 image objects are not necessarily removed with the row.

**Note** — `requestMap.get("id")` is cast directly to `String`, so sending `{"id": 2}` as a JSON **number** raises a `ClassCastException` and yields the 500 below. Send the id as a quoted string.

requestBody.description: Only the `id` key is read, and it must be a JSON string.

500.description: No such letterhead for this user, `id` was not sent as a string, or the delete threw.

post.summary: Delete a Custom Salutation
post.description:
**Use this when** the user removes a greeting from their salutation list.

**Database behaviour** — removes the entry with the given `saluationID` from the `customizedSaluation` JSON column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, scoped to the JWT-resolved user.

**Side effects** — destructive and not reversible. Mails already sent with the greeting are unaffected.

**Note** — the Java method is named `deleteCustomizedInstantReply`, overloading the instant-reply handler's name. Only the mapped path `deleteCustomizedSaluation` and the `SaluationsRO` body distinguish them.

requestBody.description: `saluationID` identifies the entry to remove. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No settings row or no such entry (`msg`: "Invalid KpostID"), or the write threw.

post.summary: Delete a Canned Instant Reply
post.description:
**Use this when** the user removes a saved quick reply from their settings list.

**Database behaviour** — removes the entry with the given `id` from the `customizedInstantReply` JSON column on the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. Scoped to the JWT-resolved user, so one user cannot delete another's entry by guessing an `id`.

**Side effects** — destructive and not reversible. Mails already sent using the reply are unaffected.

requestBody.description: `id` identifies the entry to remove. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No settings row or no such entry (`msg`: "Invalid KpostID"), or the write threw.

post.summary: List Drafts Addressed to One Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** the user selects a contact in the Drafts folder — returns only the drafts addressed to that recipient, which is far cheaper than fetching all drafts and filtering client-side.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL lookup on the `Draft` table filtered by `fromAddress` (from the JWT) **and** the `toAddress` supplied in the body. Attachment details are returned inline with each draft; the attachment *binaries* remain in S3 and must be fetched separately.

**Caveat** — no matching drafts yields **HTTP 500** with inner `statusCode` `204`.

requestBody.description: Only `toAddress` is read. `fromAddress` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No drafts for that contact (inner `statusCode` 204), or the query threw.

post.summary: Save or Update a JSON Draft Mail
post.description:
**Use this when** the compose screen auto-saves, or the user explicitly clicks "Save as Draft", for a mail that carries no newly uploaded binaries. Attachments already living in S3 can still be referenced by `attachmentUuid`.

**Database behaviour** — inserts or updates a single row in the MySQL `Draft` table via `KmailDraftService.saveAsDraftMail`. If the incoming `kmailID` is non-zero the existing draft is overwritten in place, so repeated auto-saves do not accumulate rows. No MongoDB document is created: `kmailContent` is persisted on the draft row itself and only migrates to the `table_kpost_kmail_content` collection when the draft is actually sent.

**Side effects** — `fromAddress` on the payload is discarded and replaced with the `kpostID` resolved from the JWT; the call is written to the audit log under `/draftMail/`.

requestBody.description: Full compose-state payload. Meaningful fields for a draft are `toAddress`, `ccList`, `bccList`, `kmailSubject`, `kmailContent`, `saluation`, `priority`, `groupFlag` and `attachmentUuid`. Set `kmailID` to update an existing draft, or omit/zero it to create a new one. `fromAddress` is ignored — the server overwrites it from the token.

200.description: Draft persisted. `data` holds the `SentMailResponseObject` carrying the assigned `kmailID` — the client must reuse it for subsequent auto-saves.

500.description: Either the service returned no draft object (`errorMsg`: "Unable to save draft mail") or the insert threw (`errorMsg`: "Draft Letters save exception occured").

post.summary: Save a Draft Mail with Newly Uploaded Attachments
post.description:
**Use this when** the user attaches files while composing. Unlike `draftMail`, this variant accepts the binaries themselves, so the compose screen can save a draft without a separate upload round-trip.

**Database behaviour** — each uploaded file is streamed to AWS S3 by `SentMailService.sendKmailMultiPartfileUpload`, which returns `KatchupAttachment` handles; those handles plus the deserialised compose state are written to the MySQL `Draft` and draft-attachment tables. Still no MongoDB write — draft bodies stay in MySQL.

**Side effects** — S3 objects are created even if the draft insert later fails, so orphaned objects are possible. `attachmentFlag` is forced to `1` when at least one non-empty file is present, and `fromAddress` is overwritten from the JWT.

**Request shape** — `multipart/form-data` with a repeated `files` part and a `text` form field holding the JSON-encoded `SentMailRequestObject`. Note `text` is a *form field*, not a JSON body part.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: JSON-encoded `SentMailRequestObject` carrying the compose state, sent as a plain form field rather than a JSON part.

files.description: Zero or more attachment binaries. An empty first part (size 0) is treated as 'no attachments' and skips the S3 upload entirely.

200.description: Draft and its attachments persisted; `data` holds the `SentMailResponseObject` with the assigned `kmailID`.

500.description: S3 upload failed, the `text` field was not valid `SentMailRequestObject` JSON, or the draft insert returned nothing.

post.summary: Delete a Draft Mail by kmailID
post.description:
**Use this when** the user discards a draft, or immediately after a draft has been successfully sent, so it stops appearing in the drafts folder.

**Database behaviour** — `KmailDraftService.deleteDraftMailFromServer` removes the matching MySQL `Draft` row (and its attachment-detail children) scoped to both `kmailID` **and** the authenticated `fromAddress`, so one user cannot delete another user's draft by guessing an ID.

**Side effects** — destructive and not reversible. Note this method returns the service's own `ResponseEntity` unchanged, so its success envelope is produced by the service layer rather than by this controller.

requestBody.description: Only `kmailID` is required; `fromAddress` is overwritten from the JWT and every other field is ignored.

500.description: Delete threw — `errorMsg`: "Draft Letters delete got exception occured".

200.description: Draft deleted, or no matching draft existed. Envelope is generated by `KmailDraftService`.

post.summary: [Legacy] Group Follow-Up Contacts by Status
post.description:
**Superseded by `statusOfKmailsContactsWithCount`**, which returns the same grouping plus per-contact counts. The `unused` path prefix marks this one as retired.

**Database behaviour** — aggregates MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows for the authenticated user into the follow-up bucket selected by `kmailStatusFlag`. No MongoDB access.

**Status flags** — `0` sent mail not yet opened, `1` reply not received, `2` reply not sent.

**Note** — the service result is returned verbatim, so the response shape is whatever `CommonMailService` produces rather than the usual envelope.

requestBody.description: `kmailStatusFlag` selects the bucket (0/1/2). `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: Contacts grouped by follow-up status, in the service's own shape.

500.description: The aggregation threw.

post.summary: [Legacy] Sync Post-Box Contacts and Groups
post.description:
**Superseded by `knownPostBoxContacts`.** The `unused` path prefix marks it as retired; keep it only for clients that have not migrated.

**Behaviour** — has two distinct modes driven by `lastFetchTime`:
* **With `lastFetchTime`** — delta sync, returning only contacts and groups changed since that   timestamp.
* **Without `lastFetchTime`** — full sync, resolving the user, deriving every correspondent from mail   history, and returning other-domain contacts plus expanded sender details.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL only, across `Contacts`, `UserGroup`, `User` and `KmailOtherDomainContacts`. No MongoDB access. The full-sync branch is expensive: it derives sender IDs from the entire mail history, then expands each into a `User` record.

**Caveats** — unlike its replacement this endpoint reads `kpostUser` **from the request body rather than the JWT**, so it is not scoped to the caller. It also authenticates via a hardcoded literal password (`"1111111"`) when resolving the user. In delta mode an empty result returns **HTTP 500** with an inner `statusCode` of 204.

requestBody.description: `kpostUser` is required and is **not** overwritten from the JWT. Include `lastFetchTime` for a delta sync, omit it for a full sync.

200.description: Full sync returns `otherDomainContactsList`, `senderidsList` and `senderDetailedList`; delta sync returns `lastFetchedGroupDetails` and `lastFetchMyContacts`.

500.description: Delta sync found no changes (inner `statusCode` 204, empty arrays), or the sync threw.

post.summary: Group Follow-Up Contacts by Status, with Counts
post.description:
**Use this when** rendering the follow-up dashboard — returns, for the chosen status bucket, each contact together with how many mails of theirs sit in it, so the UI can show "Arun (5)" without a per-contact round trip.

**Database behaviour** — a `GROUP BY` aggregation over the authenticated user's MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows, filtered by `kmailStatusFlag`. Counts only — no mail objects and no MongoDB access. Drill into a bucket with `sentMailNotOpened`, `replyNotReceived` or `replyNotSent`.

**Status flags** — `0` sent mail not yet opened, `1` reply not received, `2` reply not sent.

**Note** — the service result is returned verbatim, so the response is the service's own map rather than the standard envelope. This endpoint supersedes `unusedstatusOfKmailsContacts`.

requestBody.description: `kmailStatusFlag` selects the bucket (0/1/2). `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: Contacts in the selected bucket with their counts.

500.description: The aggregation threw.

post.summary: Flag or Unflag Mail as Important
post.description:
**Use this when** the user stars a message. The flag is personal — it lives on the caller's own transaction rows, so starring does not reveal anything to other recipients.

**Database behaviour** — updates the importance flag on the authenticated user's MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows. A state change; no MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — the mail begins or stops appearing in `getAllImportantMails`.

requestBody.description: Identify the mail via `transactionIDs` and/or `kmailID`. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: At least one row was updated.

500.description: No rows matched, or the update threw.

post.summary: List Sent Mail the Recipient Has Not Opened
post.description:
**Use this when** the user reviews follow-ups — surfaces mail they sent to a contact that still shows no read receipt, so they can chase it.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL query over `KmailTransaction` for mail sent by the authenticated user to `selectedContact` whose recipient-side read status is still unopened (status flag `0`). Metadata only; no MongoDB access.

**Related** — `replyNotReceived` covers mail that *was* opened but never answered; this one covers mail never opened at all.

requestBody.description: Only `selectedContact` is read. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: Returned both when unopened mail exists (`data` holds the `KmailMaster` array) and when there is none (`errorValue` "No Content", no `data`). Unlike the sibling subject endpoint, the empty case is correctly a 200 here.

500.description: The query threw.

post.summary: List the Conversation with One Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** the user opens a contact and expects the full two-way thread with them — both directions of correspondence in one chronological list, rather than separate inbox and sent views.

**Database behaviour** — keyset-paginated MySQL query over `KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction` filtered to mail where the authenticated user and `selectedContact` are counterparties. Metadata only; bodies come from the MongoDB content collection via `v2/readMail`.

**Pagination** — same cursor contract as `getKmailDashboardMsg`: pass `lastKmailID` for older messages; the response echoes `firstKmailID` and `lastKmailID`. Set `groupFlag` when `selectedContact` is a group rather than an individual.

requestBody.description: `selectedContact` is required. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: Returned both when mail exists — `data` holds the `KmailMaster` array with `firstKmailID`/`lastKmailID` cursors — and when there is none, signalled by `errorCode` "There is no Mails".

500.description: The query threw.

post.summary: Record an Unsubscribe Request
post.description:
**Use this when** a recipient clicks the unsubscribe link in a bulk mail. This is the landing endpoint for that link, which is why it is deliberately public.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a row into the MySQL `KmailUnsubscriber` table recording the sender/receiver pair and the stated reason. The bulk pipeline (`postBulkMail`, `postBulkMailMultipart`) consults this table and filters unsubscribed recipients out of future campaigns. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — suppresses future bulk mail from that sender to that receiver. One-to-one mail is **not** affected.

**Security note** — this path is `permitAll` in `SecurityConfiguration` (`/v2/common/saveUnsubscriberDetails/**`), and both `sender` and `receiver` come from the request body with no token binding or ownership check. Anyone can therefore unsubscribe any address from any sender. That openness is required for click-through unsubscribe links to work without a login, but it means the endpoint should be rate-limited and the link ideally carry a signed token.

requestBody.description: `sender` is the campaign sender being unsubscribed from and `receiver` the address opting out. `reason` is free text. `id` and the audit timestamps are assigned server-side.

500.description: The service returned nothing, or the insert threw.

post.summary: List Received Mail the User Still Owes a Reply To
post.description:
**Use this when** building the user's own to-do list — mail *they* received from a contact and have read but not yet answered.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL query over `KmailTransaction` for mail received by the authenticated user from `selectedContact` carrying the "reply not sent" status (flag `2`), excluding threads cleared via `replyNotRequiredByReceiver`. Metadata only; no MongoDB access.

**Related** — the mirror of `replyNotReceived`: that one lists replies *owed to* the user, this one lists replies *owed by* them.

requestBody.description: Only `selectedContact` is read. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: `data` holds the `KmailMaster` array, or `errorValue` is "No Content" when nothing is pending.

500.description: The query threw.

post.summary: Mark Threads as Needing No Reply (Sender Side)
post.description:
**Use this when** the user, as sender, decides they are no longer waiting on a response — this clears the selected mail out of their `replyNotReceived` follow-up list.

**Database behaviour** — updates the reply-required flag on the matching MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows for the authenticated sender. A **state change, not a read**; no MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — permanently removes the mail from the sender's follow-up bucket. The recipient's own `replyNotSent` obligation is unaffected — clearing your expectation does not clear their task.

requestBody.description: Identify the affected mail via `transactionIDs` (and/or `kmailID`/`selectedContact`). `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: **No rows matched** — unknown IDs, or mail not owned by the caller — or the update threw. A no-op update is reported as a failure, not a success.

200.description: At least one row was updated.

post.summary: Dismiss a Reply Obligation (Receiver Side)
post.description:
**Use this when** the user, as recipient, decides a mail needs no answer — the equivalent of clearing a task. It removes the mail from their `replyNotSent` list.

**Database behaviour** — updates the reply-required flag on the matching MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows for the authenticated receiver. A state change; no MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — permanently dismisses the obligation. The sender's `replyNotReceived` view is unaffected — they continue to see the mail as awaiting a reply.

requestBody.description: Identify the affected mail via `transactionIDs` (and/or `kmailID`/`selectedContact`). `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: At least one row was updated.

500.description: No rows matched, or the update threw.

post.summary: List Sent Mail Awaiting a Reply
post.description:
**Use this when** the user chases outstanding responses — surfaces mail they sent to a contact that has been opened but not yet answered.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL query over `KmailTransaction` for mail sent by the authenticated user to `selectedContact` carrying the "reply not received" status (flag `1`), excluding threads the sender marked as needing no reply via `replyNotRequiredBySender`. Metadata only; no MongoDB access.

**Related** — `sentMailNotOpened` covers mail never opened; `replyNotSent` is the inverse, listing mail *the user themselves* owes a reply to.

requestBody.description: Only `selectedContact` is read. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: The query threw.

200.description: `data` holds the `KmailMaster` array, or `errorValue` is "No Content" when nothing is outstanding.

post.summary: List Distinct Subjects Exchanged with a Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** offering a subject filter or thread picker for a conversation — lets the user narrow a long history to one topic without downloading every message first.

**Database behaviour** — a projection query returning distinct `kmailSubject` values from MySQL for mail between the authenticated user and `selectedContact`. Returns **strings only**, not mail objects; no MongoDB access.

**Caveat** — an empty result returns **HTTP 500** with an inner `statusCode` of 204 and `errorValue` "No Content". A contact with no correspondence is a normal state but is reported as an error.

requestBody.description: Only `selectedContact` is read. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No subjects found (inner `statusCode` 204), or the query threw.

post.summary: Sync External Contacts (Full or Incremental)
post.description:
**Use this when** the client refreshes its local contact cache. Replaces the retired `unusedpostBoxContacts` and, unlike it, scopes results to the JWT-resolved user.

**Two modes, chosen by `lastFetchTime`:**
* **Omitted → full sync.** Returns every `KmailOtherDomainContacts` row for the user under   `otherDomainContacts_added`.
* **Supplied → delta sync.** Returns only rows created or modified since that timestamp, split across   `otherDomainContacts_added` and `otherDomainContacts_updated`.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL queries against `KmailOtherDomainContacts` filtered on `createdDate` / `modifiedDate`. No MongoDB access.

**Cursor** — every response carries `lastFetchDate`, a server-generated timestamp. Persist it and send it back as `lastFetchTime` on the next sync.

**Known gap** — deletions are computed by the service but the `otherDomainContacts_deleted` key is **commented out**, so soft-deleted contacts are never reported to clients. A delta sync alone will not converge; periodically run a full sync to drop stale entries.

**Caveat** — this handler has **no try/catch**, so a failure propagates as the container's default error response rather than the usual envelope.

requestBody.description: Send `{}` for a full sync, or `lastFetchTime` from the previous response for a delta. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: `otherDomainContacts_added` and `otherDomainContacts_updated` (each an array, empty when nothing changed) plus the `lastFetchDate` cursor for the next call.

post.summary: Get Per-Member Read Status for a Group Mail
post.description:
**Use this when** the sender of a group mail wants to see which members have opened it — the group analogue of `getCopiesInfo`, answering "who has read this?" across a distribution list.

**Database behaviour** — reads the MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows generated for each group member when the mail was sent (one row per recipient) and reports each member's individual read state. Metadata only; no MongoDB access.

**Note** — the service's `ResponseEntity` is returned unchanged, so the success envelope is produced by the service layer.

requestBody.description: `kmailID` identifies the group mail; set `groupFlag` and `selectedContact` to the group. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: Unknown group mail, caller not the sender, or the query threw. Note the error envelope on this path is mislabelled with `urlPath` "ClearstatusOfKmailsContacts".

200.description: Per-member read status; envelope produced by `CommonMailService`.

post.summary: Fetch Messages Newer Than a Cursor (Incremental Refresh)
post.description:
**Use this when** polling for new mail while the mailbox is already open. Pass the newest ID the client currently holds and only mail *above* it comes back — much cheaper than re-fetching page one and diffing.

**Database behaviour** — a forward keyset MySQL query over `KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction` returning rows whose `kmailID` exceeds the supplied cursor. Metadata only; bodies live in the MongoDB content collection.

**Pagination** — the mirror image of `getKmailDashboardMsg`: that endpoint walks backwards into history, this one walks forwards into new arrivals. Send `firstKmailID` (or `lastKmailID`) as the high-water mark.

**Caveat** — when nothing new is found the handler falls past the `if` block and returns an **HTTP 200 with an empty body** carrying no `status` or `statusCode` at all. Treat an empty object as 'no new mail', not as an error.

requestBody.description: Supply the newest `kmailID` the client already holds as the cursor. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

200.description: `kmail` holds any newer `KmailMaster` rows and `kmailID` the new high-water mark. An **empty body** means nothing new arrived.

500.description: The query threw; `errorValue`: "While getting Kmail Dashboard Message exception occured".

post.summary: Load a Page of Dashboard (Inbox) Messages
post.description:
**Use this when** rendering the main mailbox list and when the user scrolls for older mail. This is the primary listing call.

**Database behaviour** — a keyset-paginated MySQL query over `KmailMaster` joined to `KmailTransaction` for the authenticated user, ordered by `kmailID` and limited by `count` (**default 50** when omitted). **Metadata only** — subjects, participants, flags and timestamps. Mail bodies are not included and must be fetched per-mail from the MongoDB content collection via `POST /v2/readMail/sentAndInboxMailContent`.

**Pagination** — seek-based, not offset-based. Send `lastKmailID` from the previous response to fetch the next older page; the response echoes `firstKmailID` and `lastKmailID` as the cursors for the page just returned. `fetchMailType` filters by read state: `Y` opened, `N` unopened, `A` all.

**Side effects** — none; listing does not mark anything read.

requestBody.description: `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT. Omit both cursors for the first page.

500.description: The query threw; `errorValue`: "While getting Kmail Dashboard Message exception occured".

200.description: Returned both when mail was found — `kmail` holds the `KmailMaster` array plus `firstKmailID`/`lastKmailID` cursors — and when the page is empty, in which case `errorMsg` is "No Data Found" and no cursors are present. Absence of cursors is the end-of-list signal.

post.summary: Load a Page of Bulk-Campaign Messages
post.description:
**Use this when** rendering the bulk/newsletter folder. Identical contract to `getKmailDashboardMsg` but scoped to mail sent through the bulk pipeline, so high-volume campaigns do not flood the normal mailbox view.

**Database behaviour** — the same keyset-paginated MySQL query over `KmailMaster`/`KmailTransaction`, additionally filtered to bulk-originated mail. Metadata only; bodies come from the MongoDB content collection via `v2/readMail`.

**Pagination** — identical to `getKmailDashboardMsg`: pass `lastKmailID` to page backwards through older mail; `count` defaults to 50.

requestBody.description: `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT. Omit cursors for the first page.

200.description: Either `kmail` plus the `firstKmailID`/`lastKmailID` cursors, or `errorMsg` "No Data Found" for an empty page.

500.description: The query threw; `errorValue`: "While getting Bulk Kmail Dashboard Message exception occured".

post.summary: Get Mail Counts, Overall or for One Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** the UI needs folder totals — either mailbox-wide, or scoped to the conversation with a single contact or group so the header can show "142 messages".

**Database behaviour** — `COUNT` aggregations over the authenticated user's MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows, optionally narrowed by `selectedContact`. Counts only — no mail objects and no MongoDB access, which makes this much cheaper than fetching a page and reading its length.

**Scope** — omit `selectedContact` (or send null) for mailbox-wide totals; supply it, with `groupFlag` set appropriately, for a single conversation.

**Note** — the body values are cast directly, so `selectedContact` must be a JSON **string** and `groupFlag` a JSON **boolean**; sending `"true"` as a string raises a `ClassCastException` and produces the 500 below.

requestBody.description: Free-form object; only `selectedContact` (string, optional) and `groupFlag` (boolean) are read. The user comes from the JWT.

500.description: The service returned an empty map, a body value had the wrong JSON type, or the aggregation threw.

post.summary: List Mail Flagged Important
post.description:
**Use this when** rendering the Starred/Important folder.

**Database behaviour** — MySQL query over the authenticated user's `KmailTransaction` rows filtered on the importance flag, joined back to `KmailMaster`. Metadata only; bodies come from the MongoDB content collection via `v2/readMail`.

**Response shape** — `data` is a **`Set`, not a `List`**, so ordering is not guaranteed to be chronological. Sort client-side on `kmailID` or send date if order matters.

requestBody.description: `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT; remaining filters are optional.

500.description: Nothing is flagged important, or the query threw. An empty folder is reported as an error rather than an empty list.

post.summary: Update an External Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** the user renames an external contact, changes its reference label, or toggles the blocked/subscribe flags.

**Database behaviour** — updates the matching MySQL `KmailOtherDomainContacts` row, scoped to both `id` and the authenticated `kpostID`, so one user cannot edit another's contact by guessing an id. The change is stamped into `modifiedDate`, which is what makes it visible to the delta sync in `knownPostBoxContacts`. No MongoDB access.

requestBody.description: `id` identifies the contact; send the full record with updated values. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No such contact for this user, or the update threw.

post.summary: Delete an External Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** the user removes an external contact from their address book.

**Database behaviour** — a **soft delete**: sets `deleteStatus` on the matching MySQL `KmailOtherDomainContacts` row rather than removing it, scoped to the authenticated `kpostID`. Retaining the row is what allows the delta sync in `knownPostBoxContacts` to tell clients that the contact disappeared. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — the contact stops appearing in pickers. Mail already exchanged with the address is untouched and the correspondent will still surface under `miscellaneousContacts`.

requestBody.description: `id` identifies the contact to remove. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No such contact for this user, or the delete threw (`errorCode`: "unable to delete").

post.summary: Delete Mail for the Current User Only
post.description:
**Use this when** the user deletes one or more messages from their mailbox.

**Database behaviour** — a **per-user soft delete**: it stamps a deleted-by marker on the caller's own MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows rather than removing the `KmailMaster` record. Because each recipient has their own transaction row, deleting hides the mail from this user while leaving every other party's copy intact.

**MongoDB** — the body document in `table_kpost_kmail_content` is deliberately **left in place**, since other recipients still need it. Deleting mail therefore reclaims no MongoDB storage.

**Side effects** — the mail disappears from this user's folders, counts and searches. Set `groupFlag` when deleting group mail.

requestBody.description: `transactionIDs` lists the transaction rows to hide — not `kmailID`s. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: No rows matched — unknown IDs, or rows not belonging to the caller — or the update threw. Note the error message on this path is mislabelled "Reply Not Required By Receiver exception occured".

200.description: At least one transaction row was marked deleted.

post.summary: Render a Mail as a PDF Document
post.description:
**Use this when** the user exports, prints or archives a mail — the service composes the header, participants, body and attachment list into a PDF via iText/PDFBox.

**Database behaviour** — none directly. Unusually for this API, the endpoint is **stateless with respect to storage**: the entire document is built from the payload you send, so the caller must first gather the mail (typically via `POST /v2/readMail/sentAndInboxMailContent`, which is what pulls the body out of MongoDB) and pass the content in here.

**Caveats** — the handler has **no try/catch and no authentication use**: it reads no `kpostID`, so it renders whatever content it is given, and a rendering failure propagates as the container's default error page rather than the usual envelope.

requestBody.description: A fully-populated mail document. `kmailContent` carries the HTML body; `attachmentNames` is listed on the PDF but the binaries are not embedded.

200.description: The service's result map, carrying the generated PDF reference or its encoded bytes.

post.summary: Clear a Follow-Up Status for Selected Mail
post.description:
**Use this when** the user dismisses specific follow-up items — for example marking a handful of chased mails as resolved so they leave the `replyNotReceived` bucket.

**Database behaviour** — updates the status flags on the authenticated user's matching MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows, narrowed by `transactionIDs` and `selectedContact`. A state change; no MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — the affected mail leaves the follow-up bucket and the counts from `statusOfKmailsContactsWithCount` drop accordingly. It does not delete anything or change read state.

**Related** — `clearStatusOfAllKmailsContacts` performs the same clear across the whole bucket without an ID list.

**Note** — the service's `ResponseEntity` is returned unchanged, so the success envelope comes from the service layer.

requestBody.description: `kmailStatusFlag` picks the bucket (0/1/2), `selectMailType` the mail category, and `transactionIDs`/`selectedContact` narrow the target. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: The update threw; `errorCode`: "clear mails exception occured".

post.summary: Clear a Follow-Up Status for All Mail in the Bucket
post.description:
**Use this when** the user hits "Clear all" on a follow-up bucket — the bulk counterpart of `clearStatusOfKmailsContacts`, which needs an explicit ID list.

**Database behaviour** — a single sweeping update across **every** matching MySQL `KmailTransaction` row for the authenticated user in the given `kmailStatusFlag` bucket. No `transactionIDs` and no contact filter are applied, so the blast radius is the whole bucket. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — irreversible in bulk: the bucket empties in one call and the individual items cannot be selectively restored. Prefer `clearStatusOfKmailsContacts` when the user selected specific mails.

**Note** — the service's `ResponseEntity` is returned unchanged.

requestBody.description: `kmailStatusFlag` picks the bucket (0/1/2) and `selectMailType` the mail category. `kpostUser` is overwritten from the JWT.

500.description: The bulk update threw; `errorCode`: "clear mails exception occured".

post.summary: Add an External (Non-KPOST) Contact
post.description:
**Use this when** the user saves someone who has no KPOST account — a Gmail or corporate address — so they can be picked from the recipient list and shown with a friendly name instead of a bare address.

**Database behaviour** — inserts a row into the MySQL `KmailOtherDomainContacts` table owned by the authenticated `kpostID`. Contacts are per-user, not global. No MongoDB access.

**Side effects** — the contact immediately appears in `knownPostBoxContacts` sync results. Setting `blockedContactFlag` suppresses mail from that address.

requestBody.description: `contactEmailID` is the external address and `contactName` its display name. `kpostID` is overwritten from the JWT; `id` is assigned by the database.

500.description: The service returned an empty result — for example a duplicate or invalid address — or the insert threw.

post.summary: [Legacy] Send a Mail with Newly Uploaded Attachments
post.description:
**Use this when** maintaining an older client already pointed at `/sentMail/postMailMultiPart/`. For anything new use `POST /v2/sentMail/postMailMultiPart/` instead — the logic is identical and only this controller's audit logging is absent.

**Database behaviour** — same dual write as the v2 endpoint: attachments to AWS S3, a `KmailMaster` row plus one `KmailTransaction` per recipient in MySQL, and one body document in the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content` keyed by `kmail_id`.

**Side effects** — sending is irreversible; `attachmentFlag` is forced to `1` when a non-empty file is present; `fromAddress` is overwritten from the JWT. Unlike the v2 controller, this handler does **not** write an audit record.

**Request shape** — `multipart/form-data`: a repeated `files` part plus a `text` **form field** holding the JSON-encoded `SentMailRequestObject`.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: JSON-encoded `SentMailRequestObject`, sent as a plain form field rather than a JSON part.

files.description: Attachment binaries. An empty first part (size 0) means 'no attachments'.

500.description: S3 upload failed, `text` was not valid `SentMailRequestObject` JSON, or the service returned an empty recipient list.

get.summary: Poll and Ingest Mail Received from External Domains
get.description:
**Use this when** the client refreshes the inbox. External senders (Gmail, corporate domains, and so on) do not write into KPOST directly — this endpoint connects to the backing mail server, pulls anything new for the authenticated user, and materialises it as native KMail records.

**Database behaviour** — this is a *write* despite being a `GET`. Each fetched message is converted into a MySQL `KmailMaster` + `KmailTransaction` pair, its body is inserted into the MongoDB `table_kpost_kmail_content` collection, and its attachments are uploaded to S3. Already-ingested messages are skipped, so repeat calls are idempotent.

**Side effects** — mutates state and performs network I/O against the mail server, so latency is much higher than a normal read. Not safe to call concurrently for the same user.

200.description: Returned both when new mail was ingested (`data` holds the `KmailMaster` array, inner `statusCode` 200) and when there was nothing new (empty `data`, inner `statusCode` 204, `msg` "New Received mail not found!").

500.description: Mail-server connection failed, or ingestion threw mid-write.

get.summary: Check Bulk Campaign Progress for a Sender
get.description:
**Use this when** polling after `postBulkMail` or `postBulkMailMultipart`, to drive a progress indicator and to learn which recipients failed.

**Database behaviour** — aggregates `KmailTransaction` delivery states in MySQL for the given sender and returns per-status counts. Read-only; the mail body in MongoDB is never touched.

**Note** — the sender is read from the **path**, not from the JWT, so this operation does not scope results to the caller. Any authenticated user can inspect another sender's campaign progress by supplying their address. Exceptions are not caught here — a failure surfaces as the container's default error response rather than the usual envelope.

parameters.name: fromAddress
parameters.description: KPOST ID / email address of the campaign sender. Not an ObjectId — bulk state is tracked in MySQL, keyed by address.

500.description: Aggregation failed; returned as the container's default error body, not the standard envelope.

200.description: Per-status delivery counts for the sender's most recent campaign.

get.summary: Stream Audio/Video Attachment Content
get.description:
**Use this when** the client plays a media attachment inline. Unlike `download`, the payload is returned as a stream suitable for progressive playback rather than buffered whole.

**Database behaviour** — no database access; streams the object from S3 through `ReadKmailService.multiPartStreamURl`, scoped to the calling `kpostID`.

**Note** — unlike the other binary endpoints, this one *does* require an `Authorization` header: the handler explicitly rejects the request with 500 when the header is absent, before any streaming begins.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: S3 object key of the media attachment — a UUID v4 assigned at upload time.

500.description: Missing `Authorization` header, unknown UUID, or the stream could not be opened. Empty body.

get.summary: List Who Received a Mail and in Which Capacity
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the "Details / Copies" panel of an open mail — it reveals the To, CC and BCC recipients and each one's delivery and read state.

**Database behaviour** — groups the MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows for the given `kmailID` by recipient role and returns them keyed by capacity. No MongoDB access — recipient information is relational metadata, not part of the stored body.

**Side effects** — none. BCC visibility is filtered against the calling `kpostID`, so a BCC recipient is not disclosed to other recipients.

parameters.name: kmailID
parameters.description: Numeric KMail identifier from `KmailMaster.kmailID` — a MySQL auto-increment `long`, **not** a 24-character Mongo ObjectId. The same value is the `kmail_id` field on the corresponding `table_kpost_kmail_content` document.

200.description: `data` maps each capacity (to/cc/bcc) to a `CopyInfoResponse` list.

500.description: Unknown `kmailID`, caller not party to the mail, or the query threw. No 404 is emitted.

get.summary: Download an Attachment Thumbnail
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering image/video previews in a mail list or attachment strip. Thumbnails are generated at upload time, so this is far cheaper than fetching the full-size original.

**Database behaviour** — no database access at all. A direct object read from the S3 `thumbnail` prefix, keyed by UUID.

**Security note** — this path is `permitAll` in `SecurityConfiguration` (`/v2/readMail/downloadThumbnail/**`) and the method takes no `HttpServletRequest`, so it performs no ownership check: anyone who knows a UUID can fetch that thumbnail. The UUID is the only secret.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: S3 object key for the thumbnail — a UUID v4 assigned at upload time. Not a Mongo ObjectId and not a database primary key.

500.description: No such key in the S3 thumbnail bucket, or the fetch threw. Empty body.

get.summary: Download a Full-Size Attachment by UUID
get.description:
**Use this when** the user downloads an attachment whose UUID is already known — from `downloadAttachment`, from `KmailMaster.attachmentPath`, or from a mail's `attachment_name` entries in the MongoDB content document.

**Database behaviour** — none. A direct object read from the S3 `attachment` prefix, streamed back as bytes.

**Security note** — the handler audits the call but performs **no ownership check** linking the UUID back to a mail the caller may read. Possession of the UUID is sufficient to retrieve the file.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: S3 object key for the attachment — a UUID v4 assigned at upload time.

500.description: No such key in the S3 attachment bucket, or the fetch threw. Empty body.

get.summary: Get the Assembled Mail Signature
get.description:
**Use this when** the compose window renders the user's signature, or when the settings screen rehydrates the signature builder. Returns every block in one object rather than requiring five separate reads.

**Database behaviour** — returns the whole `mailSignature` JSON column from the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Response shape** — an object keyed by block: `personalData`, `companyData`, `graphics`, `style`, `socialMedialink` and `templateID`. Blocks the user has never saved are simply absent, so read defensively rather than assuming all six keys exist.

500.description: The user has never saved a signature, or the read threw. An unset signature is reported as an error rather than an empty object.

get.summary: Get the Currently Active Letterhead
get.description:
**Use this when** the compose window opens and needs to render the header/footer that will be applied to the mail being written.

**Database behaviour** — reads the `letterHead` JSON column from the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row and returns only the entry currently flagged active, as a `JSONObject` converted to a plain map. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Related** — `getAllLetterHead` returns every uploaded letterhead; this returns just the active one.

500.description: No letterhead is currently active, or the read threw. 'None selected' is a normal user state but is still reported as an error here.

200.description: `data` holds the active letterhead object including the S3 URLs of its header and footer images.

get.summary: List the System-Provided Signature Templates
get.description:
**Use this when** presenting the gallery of ready-made signature layouts the user can pick from, before applying one with `saveOrUpdateMailSignatureTemplateId`.

**Database behaviour** — reads the entire MySQL `LetterHeadTemplate` table. These templates are **global, not per-user**: the query takes no `kpostID` and every user sees the same catalogue. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Response** — each `LetterHeadTemplate` carries `id`, `templateName`, the `htmlContent` skeleton the client renders, and a `logoLinks` map. Merge the user's own `getMailSignature` values into the template to preview the finished signature.

500.description: The template table is empty, or the read threw.

get.summary: Get the User's KMail Settings Record
get.description:
**Use this when** loading the settings screen or preparing the compose window — the returned `UsersKmailSetting` carries the basic signature, signature image, notification preference, saved instant replies and salutations in one call.

**Database behaviour** — a single indexed MySQL lookup, `usersKmailSettingRepo.findByKpostID`, using the `kpostID` from the JWT. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Note** — despite the name this returns the whole settings row, not just the signature. A user who has never opened settings may have no row at all, which surfaces as the 500 below rather than an empty object.

500.description: No settings row exists for this user, or the lookup threw. Both cases report `errorValue`: "There is no Messages in this Folder" — a copy-paste artefact, not a meaningful message.

get.summary: List All Letterheads the User Has Uploaded
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the letterhead picker in settings, so the user can choose which uploaded pair to activate or delete.

**Database behaviour** — reads the `letterHead` JSON array column from the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row and maps each entry to a `LetterHeadResponseObject` carrying the id and the S3 URLs of the header/footer images. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Related** — use `getLetterHead` for the single currently-active letterhead, and `getLetterHeadTemplate` for the system-provided templates shared by all users.

500.description: The user has uploaded no letterheads, or the read threw. An empty list is reported as an error rather than an empty 200.

get.summary: Get KLOUD Storage Consumption for the Authenticated User
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the storage meter in account settings, or gating a send/upload because the user is near their quota.

**Database behaviour** — aggregates the user's stored mail and attachment sizes from MySQL for the `kpostID` resolved from the JWT. Read-only; no MongoDB access — attachment byte counts are recorded relationally at upload time rather than being measured against S3 on each call.
