**Caveat — error handling** — the `catch` block is empty and falls through to `return null`, so any failure (including a **missing or invalid token**, which makes `request.getAttribute("kpostID")` null and triggers an NPE on `.toString()`) produces an empty **HTTP 200** body rather than an error envelope. Clients must treat an empty body as failure, not as zero usage.

200.description: `data` holds the `KmailDataResponse` usage breakdown. Note this handler does **not** set `status`/`statusCode`/`urlPath` — only `data`. An empty body also returns 200 and indicates a swallowed failure.

get.summary: List Distinct Recipients Across the User's Drafts
get.description:
**Use this when** the Drafts folder is grouped by contact — this powers the left-hand contact rail so the client does not have to download every draft just to derive the recipient list.

**Database behaviour** — a projection query over the MySQL `Draft` table returning distinct `toAddress` values for the authenticated sender. Returns bare KPOST IDs / email addresses, not full contact records; resolve display names separately via `v2/common/knownPostBoxContacts`.

**Caveat** — an empty result yields **HTTP 500** with inner `statusCode` `204`.

200.description: `data` holds an array of recipient identifiers.

500.description: No drafts exist (inner `statusCode` 204), or the query threw.

get.summary: List All Drafts for the Authenticated User
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the Drafts folder. Takes no input at all — the owner is derived entirely from the JWT, so a caller can only ever see their own drafts.

**Database behaviour** — a single indexed MySQL lookup on `Draft.fromAddress`, eagerly returning each draft's attachment details. No MongoDB access, no pagination: the full draft set comes back in one response.

**Caveat** — when the user has no drafts the handler returns **HTTP 500** with an inner `statusCode` of `204` and `errorMsg` "No Content". Treat the inner `status` field, not the HTTP status, as the success signal.

500.description: Empty drafts folder (inner `statusCode` 204, `errorMsg` "No Content"), or the query threw (inner `statusCode` 500).

get.summary: Get Unread Counts, Total and Per Sender
get.description:
**Use this when** driving the mailbox unread badge and the per-contact unread pips in the contact rail — one call supplies both.

**Database behaviour** — a `GROUP BY` aggregation over the authenticated user's MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows returning `(sender, count)` pairs; the controller then sums them into an overall total. No MongoDB access.

**Response shape** — `UnOpenedMailCount` is the grand total, `SenderWithCount` the per-sender breakdown as `{sender, count}` objects. Counts arrive as raw SQL numerics and are coerced through `BigInteger`, so treat them as integers rather than assuming a JSON number width.

**Freshness** — the counts change as a side effect of opening mail through `POST /v2/readMail/sentAndInboxMailContent`; re-poll after a read.

200.description: `UnOpenedMailCount` plus the `SenderWithCount` breakdown. A user with no unread mail gets a total of 0 and an empty array.

500.description: The aggregation threw; `errorMsg` carries the localised exception message.

get.summary: Get Totals for Every Follow-Up Bucket at Once
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the follow-up navigation badges — returns the totals for all three status buckets in a single call, instead of three separate `statusOfKmailsContactsWithCount` requests.

**Database behaviour** — aggregates the authenticated user's MySQL `KmailTransaction` rows across all status flags (`0` not opened, `1` reply not received, `2` reply not sent). Counts only; no mail objects and no MongoDB access.

**Note** — the service result is returned verbatim, so the response is the service's own map rather than the standard envelope.

200.description: Per-bucket totals for the authenticated user.

500.description: The aggregation threw.

get.summary: List Correspondents Not in the Address Book
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the "Others"/"Miscellaneous" bucket of the contact rail — people the user has exchanged mail with but never saved as a contact, which is what lets the UI offer "Add to contacts".

**Database behaviour** — MySQL query deriving correspondent IDs from the authenticated user's `KmailTransaction` history and subtracting those already present in `Contacts`. Returns **bare identifier strings**, not contact objects. No MongoDB access.

**Note** — the result is returned under the key `value`, not the usual `data`.

200.description: `value` holds the array of unsaved correspondent identifiers.

500.description: The query threw; `errorCode`: "There is no Messages in this Folder".

get.summary: Health-Check the Backing Mail Server
get.description:
**Use this when** diagnosing delivery problems or wiring an uptime probe — verifies that the service can actually open a session against the configured mail server.

**Database behaviour** — none. Performs outbound network I/O to the mail server only; neither MySQL nor MongoDB is touched.

**Note** — takes no `HttpServletRequest` and reads no `kpostID`, so it is effectively unauthenticated and returns no user-specific data. Latency tracks the mail server's responsiveness, so treat this as a slow probe rather than a cheap liveness check.

500.description: The connection attempt threw. Note the error envelope's `urlPath` is mislabelled "getsaluations" on this path.

200.description: Connection attempt completed; the returned map describes the outcome.

get.summary: List Salutations Available to the User
get.description:
**Use this when** populating the greeting dropdown in the compose window — returns the system defaults merged with the user's own entries saved through `v2/kmailSetting/saveOrUpdateCustomizedSaluations`.

**Database behaviour** — reads the `customizedSaluation` JSON column from the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row alongside the shared defaults. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Note** — when the JWT yields no `kpostID` the handler skips the service call entirely and returns an **empty map with HTTP 200** rather than an error, so an empty response means 'unauthenticated', not 'no salutations'.

500.description: The lookup threw.

200.description: Salutation map, or an empty object if no `kpostID` was resolved from the token.

get.summary: List the User's Canned Instant Replies
get.description:
**Use this when** rendering the one-tap quick-reply bar under an open mail. The read counterpart of `v2/kmailSetting/saveOrUpdateCustomizedInstantReply`.

**Database behaviour** — reads the `customizedInstantReply` JSON column from the user's MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row, keyed by the `kpostID` from the JWT. Read-only; no MongoDB access.

**Note** — the HTTP status is decided by inspecting the service's own `status` field, so a successful call always carries `status: SUCCESS`. If the user has no settings row the service returns a failure status and this becomes a 500.

500.description: The service reported a non-SUCCESS status — usually no settings row for this user — or the read threw.

get.summary: List the User's Most Frequent Correspondents
get.description:
**Use this when** populating "frequently contacted" shortcuts in the compose recipient picker or on the dashboard.

**Database behaviour** — two stages against MySQL: first an aggregation over the user's `KmailTransaction` history ranks correspondents by volume, then `getConatactDetails` expands the resulting IDs into display records (name, avatar). No MongoDB access.

**Response shape** — note the result appears **twice**: `frequentKmailContact` holds the enriched contact objects, while `data` holds the bare ID set they were derived from. Prefer `frequentKmailContact`; `data` is retained for older clients.

200.description: `frequentKmailContact` holds the enriched contacts; `data` holds the raw contact IDs.

500.description: The user has no correspondence history, or the aggregation threw. Note the error message on this path is mislabelled "set Letter As Important exception occured".

AttachmentCaption.description: Attachment records pairing each stored file name with its S3 UUID. Persisted to MySQL through `AttachmentCaptionListConverter` (a JPA `AttributeConverter` that serialises the list into a single column); the file *names* are additionally mirrored into the MongoDB document's `attachment_name` array.

ForwardRevealDetails.description: Details governing how much of the original sender is revealed on a forward; applies when `isRevealSource` is true.

KmailAttachments.description: Resolved attachment records (name, size, content type) built by the service during upload.

OriginalMailDetail.description: **Embedded sub-document** carrying the original mail's sender, subject and send date for replies and forwards. Persisted inside the MongoDB body document under `originalMailDetails`, so the quoted context survives even if the original mail is deleted.

kmailID.description: Mail identifier. Leave `0` when composing — the server assigns it and returns it in the response. Send a non-zero value only to update an existing draft, which overwrites it in place rather than creating a second row.

referenceKmailID.description: Identifiers of earlier mails in the thread, forming the reference chain that `POST /v2/readMail/referenceMailContent` later walks.

items.description: Identifiers of earlier mails in the thread, forming the reference chain that `POST /v2/readMail/referenceMailContent` later walks.

kmailType.description: Mail semantics, per `KPOSTConstants`: `0` normal, `1` reply, `2` share, `3` reminder, `5` note, `6` edit, `7` recall, `8` comment, `9` clarify, `14` copies, `15` forward. Replies and forwards should also set `originalKmailID` / `referenceKmailID`.

kmailSendDate.description: Send timestamp in JDBC form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`. Normally assigned by the server.

senderLatitde.description: Optional sender latitude captured at compose time.

senderLongitude.description: Optional sender longitude captured at compose time.

mailServerReferenceID.description: Upstream mail-server message reference, set when the mail originates from or is relayed through an external server.

forwardNote.description: Note typed above the quoted original when forwarding. Persisted to the MongoDB body document as `forward_note`, not to MySQL.
forwardNote.example: Passing this on for your approval.

attachmentFlag.description: Whether the mail carries attachments: `0` none, `1` present. On the multipart send endpoints the server **forces this to `1`** when a non-empty file part is received, so you do not need to set it yourself there.

groupFlag.description: Set to true when `toAddress` names a group; the service then expands group membership into one `KmailTransaction` per member.

senderName.description: Sender display name shown to recipients.

fromAddress.description: Sender. **Server-assigned on every send and draft endpoint** — overwritten with the `kpostID` from the JWT, so a value supplied here is discarded. The sole exception is `POST /v2/translator/postMail`, which is `permitAll` and honours this field as sent.

toAddress.description: Primary recipient — a KPOST ID, an external email address, or a group identifier when `groupFlag` is true.

originalKmailID.description: The mail being replied to or forwarded. Set alongside `kmailType` 1 (reply) or 15 (forward); leave `0` for an original composition.

ccList.description: Carbon-copy recipients. Each becomes its own `KmailTransaction` row and is visible to the other recipients.

items.description: Carbon-copy recipients. Each becomes its own `KmailTransaction` row and is visible to the other recipients.

bccList.description: Blind-carbon-copy recipients. Each becomes its own `KmailTransaction` row; `getCopiesInfo` filters these so they are not disclosed to other recipients.

items.description: Blind-carbon-copy recipients. Each becomes its own `KmailTransaction` row; `getCopiesInfo` filters these so they are not disclosed to other recipients.

saluation.description: Greeting token, chosen from `GET /v2/common/getSaluations`. Paired with `saluationName` to open the mail.

kmailContent.description: The mail body as an HTML fragment. **On send this is the field written to MongoDB** — it becomes `kmail_content` in the `table_kpost_kmail_content` document rather than being stored on the MySQL row. On save-as-draft it stays on the MySQL `Draft` row instead.

status.description: Outcome marker used on the response side; defaults to `FAILURE` until the send succeeds. Not meaningful as request input.

mailFlag.description: Composition mode — `new` for a fresh mail; other values mark reply/forward variants.

selectedMembers.description: For group sends, whether only selected members receive the mail (`Y`) or the whole group does (`N`).

groupReceiverList.description: Explicit member list when `selectedMembers` is `Y`, restricting a group send to these recipients.

items.description: Explicit member list when `selectedMembers` is `Y`, restricting a group send to these recipients.

draftUniqueMailID.description: Unique identifier of the draft this mail was composed from, letting the service clear that draft once the mail is sent.

attachmentUuid.description: S3 UUIDs of attachments **already uploaded**. Use this with the JSON send endpoints (`postMail`, `draftMail`); the multipart endpoints upload the files and populate the equivalent handles themselves.

items.description: S3 UUIDs of attachments **already uploaded**. Use this with the JSON send endpoints (`postMail`, `draftMail`); the multipart endpoints upload the files and populate the equivalent handles themselves.

kmailAttachmetDetails.description: Resolved attachment records (name, size, content type) built by the service during upload.

attachmentCaption.description: Caption applied to a single attachment.

attachmentCaptionDetails.description: Per-attachment captions, paired with the entries in `attachmentPath`.

attachmentPath.description: Attachment records pairing each stored file name with its S3 UUID. Persisted to MySQL through `AttachmentCaptionListConverter` (a JPA `AttributeConverter` that serialises the list into a single column); the file *names* are additionally mirrored into the MongoDB document's `attachment_name` array.

SentMailRequestObject.description:
Compose payload shared by the send and draft operations. On send, the service splits this object across two stores: the addressing and flag fields become a MySQL `KmailMaster` row plus one `KmailTransaction` per recipient, while `kmailContent`, `forwardNote` and the attachment names become a document in the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content`. On save-as-draft nothing is written to MongoDB — the body stays on the MySQL `Draft` row until the mail is actually sent.

`fromAddress` is always overwritten from the JWT, with one exception: `POST /v2/translator/postMail` sits behind a `permitAll` matcher and honours whatever sender the body specifies.

langFrom.description: Source language as an ISO 639-1 code. **Omit to auto-detect** — the service calls detectlanguage.com and fills this in. Sending a value equal to `langTo` causes the request to be rejected.

langTo.description: Target language as an ISO 639-1 code. Required, and must differ from the resolved `langFrom`.

msgToTranslate.description: The text to translate — typically a mail body.

msgAfterTranslation.description: The translated text. Populated in the response; ignored on input.
msgAfterTranslation.example: Hello, thank you for your message.

msgTranslatedFromLanguage.description: Source language actually used — the detected value when `langFrom` was omitted. Response-only.

kmailID.description: Leave `0` when composing — the server assigns identifiers per generated mail.

kmailType.description: Mail semantics, per `KPOSTConstants`; `0` (normal) is the usual value for a campaign.

kmailSubject.description: Subject line applied to every mail in the campaign.

kmailSendDate.description: Send timestamp in JDBC form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`. Normally assigned by the server.

fromAddress.description: Campaign sender. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Overwritten with the `kpostID` from the JWT, and it is this value you pass to the bulk-status endpoint.

toAddress.description: Single recipient. Normally left unset for a campaign — use `toAddressList` instead.

toAddressList.description: **The campaign recipient list.** Each entry receives its own individual mail and cannot see the other recipients. Unsubscribed addresses are removed before dispatch.

items.description: **The campaign recipient list.** Each entry receives its own individual mail and cannot see the other recipients. Unsubscribed addresses are removed before dispatch.

saluation.description: Greeting token applied to each generated mail.

kmailContent.description: Campaign body as an HTML fragment. Written once per generated mail into the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content`.

mailFlag.description: Composition mode; `new` for a fresh campaign.

attachmentUuid.description: S3 UUIDs of attachments already uploaded, shared across every mail in the campaign.

items.description: S3 UUIDs of attachments already uploaded, shared across every mail in the campaign.

BulkMailRequestObject.description: Campaign definition as a JSON part. `fromAddress` is overwritten from the JWT.

kpostID.description: KPOST account whose mail-server settings are being requested. Read from the body — **not** from the JWT.

password.description: Account password. Supply either this or `token`.

token.description: Previously issued token, as an alternative to `password`.

KmailCredentialsRequestObject.description: Request payload for `POST /v2/sentMail/getMailCredentials`. Unusually for this API the account is asserted in the body rather than derived from the JWT, and the response returns credential material — treat this payload as sensitive and never log it.

kmailID.description: Mail to read, matching `KmailMaster.kmailID` in MySQL and the `kmail_id` field of the MongoDB content document. A numeric auto-increment value, **not** a 24-character Mongo ObjectId.

kmailNumber.description: Sequence number of the mail within its conversation thread.

kpostUser.description: Owning KPOST user. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Overwritten with the `kpostID` resolved from the JWT before the service layer runs.

selectedContact.description: The counterparty in the conversation. Also drives special handling: when this contains `mailer-daemon@`, bounce bodies are rewritten to strip `<address>` angle brackets.

receiver.description: Explicit recipient address, where the reading context needs to distinguish one recipient of a multi-recipient mail.

kmailType.description: Which folder to read from — **required and must not be blank** (`@NotBlank`; a blank value yields HTTP 400 on `downloadODAttachment`). Any value containing `sent` routes to the sent-mail reader; anything else is treated as Inbox.

kmailSendDate.description: Send timestamp, in JDBC form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`.

kmailSubject.description: Subject line, used where the read is narrowed by topic.

groupFlag.description: Set to true when the mail belongs to a group conversation; on `downloadODAttachment` this switches attachment resolution to the group-aware S3 lookup.

referenceMails.description: Ordered `kmailID`s making up a reference (thread) chain, consumed by `referenceMailContent`. Each entry triggers its own MongoDB `findByKmailID` lookup, so long threads cost one round trip per mail. Defaults to an empty list.

items.description: Ordered `kmailID`s making up a reference (thread) chain, consumed by `referenceMailContent`. Each entry triggers its own MongoDB `findByKmailID` lookup, so long threads cost one round trip per mail. Defaults to an empty list.

senderUniqueMailID.description: Sender-side unique mail identifier, used to disambiguate a specific copy of a mail.

receiverUniqueMailID.description: Receiver-side unique mail identifier, used to disambiguate a specific copy of a mail.

draftKmailID.description: Identifier of a saved draft, read by `draftMailContent`. Draft bodies live on the MySQL `Draft` row — a draft has no MongoDB content document because it has never been sent.

kmailIDs.description: Batch of mail identifiers, consumed by `getKmailDetailsUsingKmailID`.

items.description: Batch of mail identifiers, consumed by `getKmailDetailsUsingKmailID`.

targetFileName.description: Display file name of the attachment to download, matched against the mail's stored attachment list to resolve its S3 UUID. Required by `downloadODAttachment`.

ReadMailRequestObject.description: Request payload for the `v2/readMail` operations. Identifies which mail (or thread, or attachment) to retrieve. The mail body itself is loaded from the MongoDB collection `table_kpost_kmail_content` by matching `kmailID` against that document's `kmail_id` field.

saluationID.description: Identifier of an existing salutation. Omit to create a new one; required when updating or deleting.

kpostID.description: Owning user. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Overwritten with the `kpostID` from the JWT.

saluation.description: The greeting text, paired at compose time with the recipient's name.

SaluationsRO.description: Payload for creating, updating and deleting a user's custom salutations. Entries are stored in the `customizedSaluation` JSON column on the MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row for the authenticated user.

id.description: Identifier of an existing instant reply. Omit to create a new one; required when updating or deleting.

kpostID.description: Owning user. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Overwritten with the `kpostID` from the JWT.

instantReplyRO.description: Payload for creating, updating and deleting a user's canned instant replies — the one-tap responses offered under an open mail. Entries are stored in the `customizedInstantReply` JSON column on the MySQL `UsersKmailSetting` row for the authenticated user.

kmailID.description: Draft identifier — a MySQL auto-increment `bigint`, not a Mongo ObjectId. Returned when the draft is first saved; send it back to update the same draft in place, or to delete it.

fromAddress.description: Owning sender. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Overwritten with the `kpostID` from the JWT, which is what scopes every draft query to the caller.

saluation.description: Greeting token chosen at compose time.

toAddress.description: Intended recipient. Also the filter used by `getDraftMailsForSelectedContact` and the value listed by `getDraftMailsContacts`.

kmailSubject.description: Subject line as typed so far.

kmailSendDate.description: Timestamp of the draft, in JDBC form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`.

cc.description: Carbon-copy recipients. Stored as a **single delimited string** on the draft row, not as the JSON array used by `SentMailRequestObject.ccList`.

bcc.description: Blind-carbon-copy recipients, likewise stored as a single delimited string.

draftMailID.description: Unique draft reference carried through to the send, so the draft can be cleared once the mail goes out.

attachmentFlag.description: Whether the draft carries attachments: `0` none, `1` present. Forced to `1` by `draftMailMultiPart` when a non-empty file part is received.

attachmentUuid.description: S3 UUIDs of the draft's attachments. Persisted into a single MySQL `json` column via `StringListConverter` rather than a child table.

items.description: S3 UUIDs of the draft's attachments. Persisted into a single MySQL `json` column via `StringListConverter` rather than a child table.

groupFlag.description: Set when `toAddress` names a group rather than an individual.

attachmentDetails.description: Resolved attachment metadata (file name, size, caption) assembled for the client. **JPA `@Transient`** — derived at read time from the S3 records rather than stored on the draft row, so it is populated on responses and ignored on input.

Draft.description: An unsent mail saved during composition. Persisted as a row in the MySQL table `TBL_KPOST_KMAIL_DRAFTS` and owned by `fromAddress`, which is always taken from the JWT. **A draft has no MongoDB content document** — unlike sent mail, its body stays on this relational row and only moves into `table_kpost_kmail_content` when the mail is finally sent.

DraftAttachmentDetails.description: Resolved attachment metadata (file name, size, caption) assembled for the client. **JPA `@Transient`** — derived at read time from the S3 records rather than stored on the draft row, so it is populated on responses and ignored on input.

firstKmailID.description: Keyset cursor for the newest mail on the current page. Send it back to `getKmailDashboardNewMsg` as the high-water mark when polling forwards for new arrivals.

lastKmailID.description: Keyset cursor for the oldest mail on the current page. Send it back to `getKmailDashboardMsg` / `selectedContactMails` to page backwards into older mail. Omit both cursors to request the first page.

kpostUser.description: Owning KPOST user. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Every controller overwrites this with the `kpostID` resolved from the JWT before the service layer sees it, so any value supplied here is discarded. (The one exception is the retired `unusedpostBoxContacts`, which does read it from the body.)

selectedContact.description: The counterparty whose conversation to act on — a KPOST ID, an external email address, or a group identifier when `groupFlag` is true.

kmailID.description: Single mail identifier, matching `KmailMaster.kmailID` in MySQL and the `kmail_id` field of the MongoDB content document. A numeric auto-increment value, **not** a Mongo ObjectId.

selectedDate.description: Optional date filter, in JDBC timestamp form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`.

groupFlag.description: Set to true when `selectedContact` names a group rather than an individual; this switches the query to expand group membership.

kmailIDs.description: Batch of mail identifiers, for operations that act on several mails at once.

items.description: Batch of mail identifiers, for operations that act on several mails at once.

fetchMailType.description: Read-state filter for listing endpoints: `Y` opened only, `N` unopened only, `A` all.

kmailStatusFlag.description: Follow-up bucket selector: `0` sent mail not yet opened by the recipient, `1` reply not received, `2` reply not sent by this user.

kmailNumber.description: Sequence number of the mail within its conversation thread.

selectMailType.description: Mail category filter used by the clear-status operations.

count.description: Page size for listing endpoints. Defaults to 50 when omitted.

transactionIDs.description: Identifiers of individual `KmailTransaction` rows — the per-recipient records, **not** `kmailID` values. Used by the delete, importance and clear-status operations so a change applies only to the caller's own copy of a mail.

items.description: Identifiers of individual `KmailTransaction` rows — the per-recipient records, **not** `kmailID` values. Used by the delete, importance and clear-status operations so a change applies only to the caller's own copy of a mail.

KmailCommonRequestObject.description: Shared request payload for most `v2/common` operations — listing, follow-up status, importance and clear actions. It is a union of every field those endpoints might need, so **any given endpoint reads only a subset**; consult the individual operation for which fields apply. Fields left unset are ignored rather than treated as filters.

lastFetchTime.description: Sync cursor. **Omit for a full sync** (every contact) or supply the `lastFetchDate` returned by the previous sync for a delta (only contacts created or modified since). JDBC timestamp form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`.

kpostUser.description: Owning KPOST user. For `knownPostBoxContacts` this is **server-assigned** and overwritten from the JWT. The retired `unusedpostBoxContacts` is the exception — it reads this field from the body and requires it.

KmailCommonRequestObjectV2.description: Request payload for the contact-sync operations (`knownPostBoxContacts`, and the retired `unusedpostBoxContacts`). Presence or absence of `lastFetchTime` is what selects between a full and an incremental sync.

id.description: Primary key of the MySQL row, assigned on insert.

sender.description: The campaign sender being unsubscribed from. Read from the request body with no token binding, because the endpoint is public so unsubscribe links work without a login.

receiver.description: The address opting out. Also unauthenticated — anyone able to reach the endpoint can submit any address, so rate-limiting or a signed link token is advisable.

reason.description: Free-text reason captured from the unsubscribe form.

createdBy.description: Audit field — who created the row. Server-assigned.

createdDate.description: Audit timestamp of the opt-out. Server-assigned.

modifiedBy.description: Audit field — who last modified the row. Server-assigned.

modifiedDate.description: Audit timestamp of the last change. Server-assigned.

KmailUnsubscriber.description: A recorded opt-out of bulk mail from one sender to one recipient. Persisted as a row in the MySQL table `TBL_KPOST_KMAIL_UNSUBSCRIBER_LIST`, which the bulk pipeline consults to filter recipients before dispatch. Suppression applies to **bulk campaigns only** — ordinary one-to-one mail between the same two parties is unaffected.

id.description: Primary key of the MySQL row — a `bigint` auto-increment identity value, **not** a Mongo ObjectId. Assigned on insert; required when editing or deleting.

kpostID.description: Owning KPOST user. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Every operation overwrites this with the `kpostID` from the JWT, which is what makes contacts per-user rather than global.

contactEmailID.description: The external (non-KPOST) email address this contact represents.

contactName.description: Display name shown in place of the bare address throughout the UI.

referenceName.description: Free-text label for grouping or recall, such as a company or relationship.

blockedContactFlag.description: When true, mail from this address is suppressed for the owning user.

deleteStatus.description: Soft-delete marker. `deleteOtherDomainContact` sets this rather than removing the row, so the record survives to inform delta syncs. **Note** the deletion list is currently commented out of the `knownPostBoxContacts` response, so soft-deleted contacts are not reported to clients — a periodic full sync is needed to drop them.

subscribe.description: Whether this contact is opted in to bulk mail from the owning user.

createdBy.description: Audit field — who created the row. Server-assigned.

createdDate.description: Audit timestamp, defaulted to insert time. Compared against `lastFetchTime` to decide which contacts are reported as *added* by a delta sync.

modifiedBy.description: Audit field — who last modified the row. Server-assigned.

modifiedDate.description: Audit timestamp of the last edit. Compared against `lastFetchTime` to decide which contacts are reported as *updated* by a delta sync.

KmailOtherDomainContacts.description: A contact outside the KPOST domain — someone with no KPOST account, saved so they can be addressed by name. Persisted as a row in the MySQL table `TBL_KPOST_KMAIL_OTHER_DOMAIN_CONTACTS`; this is a JPA entity, not a MongoDB document. Contacts are scoped per user via `kpostID`, and deletion is soft (`deleteStatus`) so that incremental syncs can observe the change.

kpostUser.description: Owning KPOST user. **Server-assigned — do not send.** Overwritten with the `kpostID` resolved from the JWT, which is what confines the delete to the caller's own copies.

groupFlag.description: Set to true when deleting group mail, so the group-aware transaction rows are targeted.

transactionIDs.description: Identifiers of the `KmailTransaction` rows to hide — the per-recipient records, **not** `kmailID` values. Passing a `kmailID` here will match nothing and the call reports failure.

items.description: Identifiers of the `KmailTransaction` rows to hide — the per-recipient records, **not** `kmailID` values. Passing a `kmailID` here will match nothing and the call reports failure.

DeleteKmailRequestObject.description: Request payload for `deleteKmailWithDeletedBy`. Deletion is a per-user soft delete: it stamps a deleted-by marker on the caller's own `KmailTransaction` rows in MySQL, leaving both the shared `KmailMaster` record and the MongoDB body document intact for the other parties to the mail.

fromAddress.description: Sender shown in the PDF header. Not validated against the caller's identity.

toAddress.description: Primary recipient shown in the PDF header.

kpostID.description: KPOST account the export is attributed to.

ccList.description: Carbon-copy recipients listed in the PDF header.

items.description: Carbon-copy recipients listed in the PDF header.

bccList.description: Blind-carbon-copy recipients. Include only when exporting the sender's own copy — these are not disclosed to other recipients elsewhere in the API.

items.description: Blind-carbon-copy recipients. Include only when exporting the sender's own copy — these are not disclosed to other recipients elsewhere in the API.

attachmentNames.description: Attachment file names listed in the PDF. **Names only — the binaries are not embedded** in the generated document.

items.description: Attachment file names listed in the PDF. **Names only — the binaries are not embedded** in the generated document.

kmailSubject.description: Subject line rendered as the document title.

kmailNumber.description: Sequence number of the mail within its thread.

kmailSendDate.description: Send timestamp shown in the header, in JDBC form `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS`.

kmailContent.description: The mail body as an HTML fragment — rendered into the PDF by iText/PDFBox. This is the value you retrieved from the MongoDB content document.

kmailType.description: Folder the mail came from, used to label the export.

MailPDFConverterRequestObject.description: Payload for `POST /v2/common/convertMailAsPDF`. The endpoint is **stateless with respect to storage** — it renders exactly what you send and looks nothing up, so the caller must first assemble the mail (typically via `POST /v2/readMail/sentAndInboxMailContent`, which is what pulls the body out of MongoDB) and pass the complete document here.

bearerAuth.description: JWT issued by the KPOST auth service. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The filter may return a refreshed token in the `Authorization` response header.
